newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German January Ifo index.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German January Ifo index.

text.p: The following are comments made by economists and analysts on Reuter Financial TV following the results of the latest Ifo survey, which showed a rise in the west German business climate index to 93.3 in January from 90.9 in December.

JUERGEN PFISTER, SENIOR ECONOMIST, COMMERZBANK: Certainly the figure is much stronger than expected. Especially because of the weather conditions in the construction sector and depressed winter sales, we were expecting a lower figure.

But this shows that the dip in the index seen in November and December did not signal a new trend, but was only temporary. Certainly all the expectations for 2.5 percent growth this year urgently need some good news, but there is no reason to revise up forecasts.

SONJA GIBBS, BOND STRATEGIST, NOMURA: The market consensus for both (the earlier published) M3 and the Ifo index was much weaker. It shows that we do have a fairly strong cyclical recovery and we are seeing the effect of the weaker mark. I think we did expect sentiment to improve, we just didn't expect it for this particular month.

GERNOT NERB, SENIOR ECONOMIST, SALOMON BROTHERS: This shows that the German economy is on track after a temporary weakness. There is no reason to alter the forecast of 2.25 percent GDP growth this year. The Bundesbank will keep rates on hold as long as possible since there is no inflationary pressure and the economy is too weak for a rate hike.
